gitCommitNote: This is the source tree commit (Phase 3.8.6's own commit) the Phase 3.8.6.1 rebuild was performed against, before Phase 3.8.6.1's own commit (which adds this manifest update) exists. Phase 3.8.6.1 fixes a real Environment C failure the operator hit installing the Phase 3.8.6 artifact: 'cip-desktop.exe - System Error: The code execution cannot proceed because libstdc++-6.dll was not found.' runtimeDependencyProof.peImportInspection: x86_64-w64-mingw32-objdump -p against the built cip-desktop.exe lists libstdc++-6.dll as a genuine dynamic import, alongside only standard Windows system DLLs (KERNEL32, user32, ole32, etc.) and WebView2Loader.dll (already handled by Tauri's own NSIS generation). objdump run again against libstdc++-6.dll itself shows it further depends on libgcc_s_seh-1.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll, and objdump against those two shows no further non-system dependencies - the complete, closed set is exactly these three DLLs.
runtimeDependencyProof.installerExtractionProof: The packaged NSIS installer was extracted directly with 7z and inspected: libstdc++-6.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll, and libwinpthread-1.dll are all present at the installer root (the same directory cip-desktop.exe installs into, $INSTDIR - confirmed via the generated installer.nsi's `File` directives, placed after `SetOutPath $INSTDIR` alongside cip-desktop.exe and WebView2Loader.dll, with matching `Delete` entries in the uninstaller section). This is now an automated, build-time-enforced check inside scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh, not a one-off manual verification.
runtimeDependencyProof.dllSourceAndArchitecture: All three DLLs were resolved from the exact posix-threads mingw-w64-x86-64 toolchain used to build cip-desktop.exe itself (via `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++/gcc -print-file-name=<dll>`, never a hardcoded path), confirmed PE32+ x86-64 via file(1), and had debug symbols stripped (x86_64-w64-mingw32-strip --strip-debug) to keep the installer size reasonable (libstdc++-6.dll: 26.3MB -> 4.6MB) without altering their code or export tables. See pilot-evidence/3.8.6.1/build/runtime-dll-evidence.json for full SHA-256 checksums and per-DLL detail.

architectureVerification.installedApplicationBinary: cip-desktop.exe: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64 (stripped to external PDB), confirmed via `file` against target/x86_64-pc-windows-gnu/release/cip-desktop.exe - the actual application that runs after installation is genuinely x64
architectureVerification.method: file(1) run directly against both the installer and the embedded application binary in this build environment

The Phase 3.8.5 non-whisper embedded binary's exact uncompressed size was not separately recorded (only its 7,140,776-byte NSIS-compressed installer was), so no direct before/after byte comparison is claimed here - the packaged installer itself still grew by ~472KB (7,140,776 -> 7,613,226 bytes) despite NSIS compression, and the symbol-strings proof below is the stronger, unambiguous evidence

provenance.builtDuring: Phase 3.8.6 (Windows Whisper Build & Packaging Audit) - the operator's Phase 3.8.5 real-Windows re-test confirmed audio capture now genuinely works (SIGNAL CAPTURED, correct listening lifecycle) but isolated the remaining blocker to transcription itself ('SPEECH ERROR'). The audit (docs/phase-3-8-6-audit.md) confirmed the root cause the operator suspected: no Windows build in this project's history has ever been compiled with the `whisper` Cargo feature, so no prior installer could ever transcribe regardless of hardware. Compiling with --features whisper for this exact cross-compilation target (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, from Linux) hit two independent, real, verified toolchain/upstream defects that had to be fixed before a working build was even possible: (1) whisper.cpp's vendored `ggml` CMake build unconditionally strips the 'lib' prefix from its own static library output for any Windows target (assuming MSVC naming), but the actual linker here is MinGW's GNU ld, which requires the Unix 'libX.a' convention for a plain -lX flag - so ggml.a/ggml-base.a/ggml-cpu.a were built but never found; (2) this container's default x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc/g++ alternative is the win32-threading-model variant, but whisper.cpp/ggml link against pthread and expect POSIX threading, producing 'undefined reference to __mingwthr_key_dtor' at final link - fixed by switching to the already-installed posix-threads alternative via update-alternatives. Neither fix touches the vendored whisper-rs-sys/ggml/whisper.cpp source; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact, repeatable two-pass build process and docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md for full root-cause evidence. Separately, the audit also found and fixed a real, previously-undocumented defect that would have blocked correct transcription even with the feature/model both present: `integrations/audio` delivers AudioChunks at the capture device's own native sample rate and never resamples (by design - see its module docs), but WhisperSpeechEngine hardcoded a 16kHz assumption and the one consumer that needed to convert (handle_audio_chunk) never did - so a real Windows device negotiating 44.1kHz/48kHz (the norm for consumer WASAPI devices like Stereo Mix/Microphone Array) would have fed audio to Whisper at roughly 3x the wrong rate. Fixed by adding SpeechEngine::required_sample_rate_hz() (a new default trait method, Some(16_000) only for WhisperSpeechEngine) and a linear-interpolation resampler at the one call site that needs it. Also fixed: the real underlying model-load/inference error text (already computed by WhisperSpeechEngine and SpeechEngineError, but discarded after logging) is now retained in AppState and surfaced through the existing get_pilot_diagnostics command/System Diagnostics panel (feature compiled, model loaded, chunks received, last chunk sample rate, inferences attempted/succeeded, real last-error text) instead of the generic 'SPEECH ERROR' notice alone.
provenance.buildEnvironment: cross-compiled from Linux using rustup target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, gcc-mingw-w64 (posix-threads alternative - see whisperFeatureProof above), cmake, and nsis (makensis) via `npx tauri build --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --features whisper` after the two build.rs-external fixes described above; see scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh for the exact repeatable process
provenance.note: This artifact supersedes the Phase 3.8.5 installer (previously SHA-256 70ea056359a1dbc738b9b84bd7f2e8bbe6d6a0088bb858aeac47cddaad04b813) because this phase modified core/ai/src/speech_engine.rs (new default SpeechEngine::required_sample_rate_hz() method), ai/speech/src/whisper.rs (WhisperSpeechEngine overrides it to Some(16_000)), apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs (resample_pcm16() pure function + wired into handle_audio_chunk before feed_audio; speech/chunk/inference diagnostics counters; PilotDiagnostics gains a `speech` field), apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs (new SpeechDiagnostics struct + AppState field), apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs (create_speech_engine now returns and retains real load-error diagnostics instead of discarding them after logging), and the frontend TS mirrors/PilotDiagnosticsPanel.tsx (renders the new Whisper diagnostics). Most importantly, THIS rebuild was compiled with --features whisper for the first time - see whisperFeatureProof above. Zero new database migrations, zero new Tauri commands (get_pilot_diagnostics keeps its exact name/params; its return type gained one additive field), zero Bible/intelligence engine changes, zero event contract changes, zero capability changes, zero changes to CpalAudioEngine or the AudioEngine trait, no second audio engine, no second speech engine, no second audio meter - see docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md for the full architectural-safety diff. This is a freshly compiled build, not a copy of a prior artifact.

releaseCandidateStatement: This is the Phase 3.8.6.1 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (Windows Runtime Dependency Packaging Fix) - the first Windows installer in this project's history to genuinely bundle its required MinGW runtime DLLs (libstdc++-6.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll, libwinpthread-1.dll) alongside the `whisper`-feature build introduced in Phase 3.8.6. It is a real, verifiable build artifact - not a placeholder, not a simulation, not a fabrication - and its DLL bundling has been verified both by directly extracting and inspecting the packaged .exe (see runtimeDependencyProof above) AND by a real-Windows-hardware relaunch performed by the operator (see physicalHardwareStatement below). See docs/phase-3-8-6-1-windows-runtime-packaging.md for the full PASS breakdown and final gate - all items now CONFIRMED.
modelPackagingStatement: NO Whisper model file is bundled with this installer, and none could be obtained to bundle: this container's egress policy blocks the standard model host (huggingface.co - confirmed via a live network test returning a proxy-level connection rejection), and no ggml/gguf model file exists anywhere in this repository to embed even if bundling logic were added. This is Option D from the operator's own spec (model expected to already exist at %APPDATA%\org.churchintelligence.cip\models\ggml-tiny.en.bin, or wherever CIP_WHISPER_MODEL_PATH points) - not a defect in the path resolver (which correctly uses Tauri's own app_data_dir() API, never a cwd/dev-relative path), but a real, honestly-reported gap: an operator must place a real model file there themselves before transcription can run, even on this whisper-enabled build. No automatic download and no network dependency were added to the shipped application to work around this, per the operator's explicit instruction. This phase (3.8.6.1) did not change this in any way - it is a runtime-DLL packaging fix only. The operator's real-Windows re-test (see physicalHardwareStatement) confirms audio capture now works end-to-end on real hardware, but transcription still fails ('SPEECH ERROR') - consistent with (though not yet proven to be caused by) no model file having been placed at the expected path. Root-causing that failure with real diagnostic evidence is Phase 3.8.7's scope.
physicalHardwareStatement: CONFIRMED on real Windows hardware by the operator: this exact artifact (SHA-256 b737f72b...) was installed and launched with NO 'libstdc++-6.dll was not found' error (the defect Phase 3.8.6.1 exists to fix), the main UI and Live Service view both opened, 'Stereo Mix (Realtek(R) Audio)' was selectable, and live audio capture genuinely worked ('SIGNAL CAPTURED', input level 3%-6%). See pilot-evidence/3.8.6.1/windows/real-windows-relaunch-confirmation.json. This closes Phase 3.8.6.1's own gate in full - packaging, launch, DLL resolution, and UI/audio reachability are all confirmed on real hardware, not just Environment A/build-time. Separately (and out of this phase's scope), Whisper transcription itself still fails on this same real machine ('SPEECH ERROR - recorded, will clear on the next successful chunk') - that is Phase 3.8.7's investigation, not evidence against this phase's DLL-packaging fix, which is now fully verified end-to-end.
githubReleaseStatus: NOT CONFIGURED - no .github/workflows directory exists in this repository, and no GitHub Release has been created for this artifact. This installer is available only via this repository's working tree (release/windows/), not via GitHub Releases or any CI/CD pipeline.
obtainingWithoutDeveloperTooling: The file at release/windows/Church Intelligence Platform_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe can be copied/transferred directly (e.g. via a git clone of this repository, a direct file download, or a USB drive) to the target Windows machine and run there. Running the installer on Windows requires none of: Claude Code, Rust, Cargo, Node.js, npm, or the CIP source tree - only the .exe file itself. A real Whisper model file (see modelPackagingStatement) must be placed separately by the operator for transcription to work.
